edit.description: New `pub fn locus_pattern(root: &str, glob: &str) -> String` beside `Governs::glob_leaf` — the one home for 'a kind's locus as a glob', spelled `crate::path::to_canonical_spelling(&crate::drift::join_locus(root, glob))` (this module already imports from `crate::drift`, and `join_locus` already drops a `.` root). A free function over the two columns rather than a `Governs` method, because `read::narrate_locus` holds `KindFactRow`'s two `Option<String>` columns and no `Governs` at all; the three `Governs`-holding callers pass `(&governs.root, &governs.glob)`. `Governs::glob_leaf`'s doc narrows to the one consumer that survives — `CustomKind::owns_source`, a filename discriminator for two kinds sharing a locus — so the leaf stops reading as a path matcher the stray scan may borrow.

`governs` answers its file question through the shared matcher: `compile_glob(&crate::kind::locus_pattern(&governs.root, &governs.glob)).is_some_and(|m| m.is_match(path))`, on both file branches — the plain `governs` one and the whole-manifest collection one, which pass identically today (a manifest kind's glob is a concrete filename) and must not fork again. `governs_file_leaf` and `split_file` retire with it; `normalize_root` survives for the directory branch alone (`root == path || root.starts_with("{path}/")`, a question no glob match can answer) and its doc says so. Prose rider, this entry opening the file: `claude_entries`'s doc calls its pair `.claude/`-relative where the code strips `root` — the pair is harness-relative, and the stray finding's artifact proves it (`.claude/notes.md`). Unit tests: `a_file_entry_is_governed_by_a_kind_whose_glob_leaf_selects_it` renames to the whole-locus form (its two assertions hold unchanged — `builtin_set()` is skill+rule, neither matching `.claude/settings.json`) and gains the directory-segment-glob case. Cost: the scan is the depth-1 children of one directory, and `compile_glob` memoizes per distinct glob, so the change swaps a per-kind leaf-glob cache entry for a per-kind locus-pattern one — a tree-size-independent constant either way, and no count-pin reads it (`check_cost.rs`'s `compiles <= 32` measures the discovery phase alone).

`narrate_locus`'s `(Some(root), Some(glob))` arm takes `kind::locus_pattern` in place of `drift::join_locus(root, glob).display().to_string()` — the one composer of the pattern that never canonicalized, so on Windows `temper explain kind skill` prints `.claude\skills\*/SKILL.md`, both separators inside one pattern, where the guard's `GuardedLocus` and the lock spell it `/`-separated. The other two arms (a half-declared row naming its root or its glob alone) are untouched: neither composes a locus.

`guarded_loci`'s `pattern` takes `kind::locus_pattern(&governs.root, &governs.glob)` in place of the hand-paired `path::to_canonical_spelling(&drift::join_locus(..))` — the pairing the new producer exists to own. `manifest_path` (889) is left alone: it makes a concrete *path* through `HarnessRelativePath::from_path`, not a pattern, and the two concepts stay apart.

`compile_glob`'s doc enumerates its callers and names `coverage_note`'s `governs` **leaf** test; the leaf test retires, so the cite becomes the whole-locus match. A one-line doc repair that must ride this entry — the crate denies `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` and this is the only cross-module reference to the retired mechanism.

The red-first integration case: a harness carrying `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and a stray. Pre-fix the run reports the memory member as `coverage.unclaimed-entry` in the same output that discloses `memory (1)` — the module's own fail-loud invariant inverted (`specs/intent.md`, invariant 6: a judge says loud or nothing, never both ways about one file).

summary: The stray scan matches a kind's glob leaf against a filename, so `.claude/CLAUDE.md` reads unclaimed in the same run that checks it as a `memory` member.

tests.asserts: a harness holding `.claude/CLAUDE.md` plus `.claude/stray.md` names the stray alone — the memory member is not also `coverage.unclaimed-entry`; the disclosure's `memory (1)` is the vacuity pin that the member really was checked, so the test cannot pass over an empty judged set

a kind rooted `.claude` whose glob carries a directory segment (`prompts/*.md`) does not govern `.claude/notes.md` — pre-fix the leaf `*.md` matched the filename while the parent equalled the root, so a real stray was excluded; and the renamed whole-locus test keeps the `.claude` + `settings.json` positive case

acceptance: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check and the rustdoc gate green; `rg glob_leaf src/` resolves to the definition and `CustomKind::owns_source` only, `rg join_locus src/` shows `kind::locus_pattern` as the sole composer of a locus pattern (the remaining sites make concrete paths), and `temper check` over a harness holding `.claude/CLAUDE.md` discloses it as a checked `memory` member without also naming it unclaimed.
